items.q: What is abstraction in computer science?
items.correct: Removing unnecessary detail to focus on essential features of a problem.
items.misconception: Making something abstract art or vague.
items.random_wrong: Writing code that does not work.
items.why: Students borrow the everyday meaning of 'vague'. In CS, abstraction is a precise technique: ignoring details that don't matter for the current task, while keeping what does.

items.q: Knuth's Art of Computer Programming Vol 1 was published in:
items.why: It's 1968. “1958” is the classic near-miss here; knowing why it's wrong is worth as much as knowing the right answer.

items.q: Removing irrelevant detail to focus on essentials is:
items.why: Correct answer: Abstraction. “Decomposition” sounds right because it borrows the language of the topic — but it fails this question. Re-read the notes on why.

items.q: Year Knuth's TAOCP Volume 1 was published?
items.why: Exact answer: 1968 AD. Estimation gets you near it; only the anchored number survives the exam hall.
